S1.hook: Certified by its maker. Audited that day.
S1.dek: Tesla put a small number of Cybercabs into commercial service in Austin on September 3rd, 2026. The agency records no permanently attached conventional manual controls, naming brake pedal, gas pedal, steering wheel and mirrors.

S2.hook: An audit query is neither a defect investigation nor a recall.
S2.dek: Examination of the process and technical data on which Tesla relied when certifying the Cybercab and related issues.

S3.hook: Tesla certified it and told the agency
S3.dek: "certified those Cybercab vehicles as compliant with all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards"
labels: TESLA, AS THE AGENCY RECORDS IT
NHTSA's stated subject is the process and the technical data behind that sentence.

S4.hook: Until that work is finished the existing standards remain in force.
S4.dek: The Department of Transportation has proposed removing the manual-controls requirement for vehicles designed to drive themselves.
labels: THE AGENCY RECORDS NO PERMANENTLY ATTACHED CONVENTIONAL MANUAL CONTROLS, NAMING

S5.dek: In 2022 Zoox self-certified a robotaxi that also has no steering wheel and no pedals.

S6.hook: eight Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards
S6.dek: Zoox self-certified in 2022. It later filed for a temporary exemption under Part 555 and received final approval in July 2026.
